question.text: A new investor subscribes to Kaveri Macro Fund (Cat III) mid-quarter. The strategy is at 5% above HWM — i.e., the existing unit NAV of Rs. 1,050 already embeds INR 50 of gains (above a HWM of Rs. 1,000) for which performance fee has NOT yet been accrued. Performance fee is 20% of gains above HWM. If the new investor subscribes via the EQUALISATION CREDIT method (Series-of-units / equalisation), what is the INITIAL offset the new investor effectively receives versus existing investors?

answer.text: A performance-fee charge equal to 20% of Rs. 50 = Rs. 10 per unit, paid upfront
An equalisation credit equal to 20% of Rs. 50 = Rs. 10 per unit, ensuring the new investor is not charged performance fee on gains that accrued BEFORE subscription
A 1% entry load credited to the fund
A bonus unit equal to 5% of subscription

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The equalisation CREDIT compensates a new investor for the fact that, had they subscribed via the standard unit, they would effectively be charged performance fee on gains that accrued BEFORE they entered. Here, 20% x INR 50 of pre-existing above-HWM gains = INR 10 per unit credit. This ensures new investors are only charged performance fee on incremental gains, maintaining fairness. **The Trap:** Option A inverts — an equalisation DEBIT is charged in a different scenario (subscription when NAV is BELOW HWM). Options C and D are fabricated. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D (Cat I/II) uses drawdown-waterfall — no equalisation concept. XIX-C / XIX-E both test Cat III equalisation. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Equalisation math is THE signature Cat III fund-accounting challenge. Use series-of-units instead if your admin can't handle equalisation accounting — both achieve fairness, simpler implementation for series-based.
